title: Blue Origin says it is building a higher-performing rocket engine at 1/4 the cost
author: Eric Berger
summary_long: KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, Fla.—Blue Origin announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket on Thursday, reducing the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expanding its capacity for payload delivery to geostationary orbit and the Moon. With these upgrades, the company aims to eventually position New Glenn to launch more than 1,000 times a year. "There has never been higher demand for launch, ever," Dave Limp, chief executive officer of Blue Origin, said during the UP.Summit conference at the Shuttle Landing Facility in Florida. title: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
author: Jeremy Hsu
summary_long: NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years. The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-05. id: space:blue origin reveals new kick stage engines for its new glenn:2026-11-05T22:34:58.000Z
title: Blue Origin reveals new kick stage, engines for its New Glenn rockets
author: Will Robinson-Smith
summary_long: Blue Origin is announced two big developments for its New Glenn rockets as the company continues to work towards its first flight following a late-May pad explosion. During an invite-only event at the Kennedy Space Center called Up.Summit, Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp announced that the company has been developing a new third stage and a new first-stage engine. This new upper stage, called Glenn Stage 3 (GS3) is designed for missions that require direct injection to geostationary orbit and Earth-escape trajectories. Blue Origin said it already has a government mission lined up for 2028 that will launch a payload to cis-lunar space, but didn’t elaborate further on that mission. Source: spaceflightnow.com. id: ai_data:reprobridge building reproducibility into ml research artifa:2026-11-05T18:45:36.000Z
title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
author: Yubo Wang
summary_long: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. title: AI learns to predict the world without ever seeing it
summary_long: Almost every artificial intelligence system we know begins in the same way: it is exposed to vast amounts of information from the real world—books, websites, images and recordings—and trained to identify patterns within it. A new study involving researchers from Tel Aviv University and Stanford University raises another possibility: Can a system develop general learning capabilities even when all the data it trains on is generated entirely from scratch within the system itself?
